title: Freezer Compartment Warm Condition
shortDescription: The freezer compartment temperature has risen above the acceptable range.
fullDescription: Error EC01 indicates the freezer compartment temperature has exceeded the high-temperature alarm threshold, typically above 15 degrees Fahrenheit. The control system monitors temperature and alerts when the freezer cannot maintain safe food storage conditions. This may be caused by compressor issues, sealed system problems, or airflow restrictions.

causes.cause: Condenser coils are dirty, reducing cooling efficiency
Compressor or start relay has failed
Door seal is worn or damaged allowing warm air in

symptoms: Food in freezer is softening or thawing
Frost or ice buildup on evaporator
Compressor runs continuously or not at all

fixSteps.title: Check the condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Sub-Zero condensers are located either above the unit or at the bottom behind the grille. Clean with a condenser brush and vacuum. Sub-Zero recommends cleaning every 6-12 months.

fixSteps.title: Check the door seal
fixSteps.instruction: Close the door on a dollar bill. If you can pull it out easily, the seal is not tight enough. Inspect the entire gasket for tears or deformation.

fixSteps.title: Listen for the evaporator fan
fixSteps.instruction: Open the freezer and listen for the evaporator fan. If silent, the fan motor may have failed. On built-in models, access the fan from inside the freezer after removing the rear panel.

fixSteps.title: Check compressor operation
fixSteps.instruction: Listen at the rear or bottom for the compressor running. If it clicks and shuts off, the start relay or compressor may be failing. If it runs but the unit is warm, there may be a refrigerant leak.

whenToCallPro: If condenser cleaning and fan check do not resolve EC01, call a Sub-Zero certified technician. Sealed system repairs require specialized equipment.

faq.q: Should I use only Sub-Zero certified technicians?
faq.a: Sub-Zero recommends using their certified service network (Certified Factory Service) to maintain warranty and ensure proper repair with genuine parts.

faq.q: How often should I clean the condenser?
faq.a: Sub-Zero recommends cleaning the condenser every 6-12 months, or more frequently in homes with pets or high dust environments.

faq.q: Can EC01 occur from simply loading too much warm food?
faq.a: Yes. Adding a large amount of room-temperature food can temporarily raise the freezer temperature enough to trigger EC01. Allow time for the unit to recover.

title: Refrigerator Compartment Warm Condition
shortDescription: The refrigerator compartment temperature has risen above the acceptable range.
fullDescription: Error EC02 indicates the fresh food (refrigerator) compartment has exceeded its high-temperature alarm threshold, typically above 45 degrees Fahrenheit. Similar to EC01 for the freezer, this alarm protects food safety by alerting to cooling failures in the refrigerator section.

causes.cause: Air damper between freezer and refrigerator is stuck closed
Evaporator fan in the refrigerator section has failed
Refrigerator section compressor has failed (dual-compressor models)
Door left open or seal is damaged

symptoms: Freezer may still be cold (dual-compressor models)

fixSteps.title: Check the door
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the refrigerator door closes fully and the seal is intact. Check that no items inside are preventing the door from closing completely.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser coils
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the condenser with a brush and vacuum. A dirty condenser is the most common cause of cooling failures.

fixSteps.title: Check the air damper
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the air damper that controls cold air flow from the freezer to the refrigerator section. It should open and close in response to the thermostat. If stuck, it may need replacement.

fixSteps.title: Verify compressor operation
fixSteps.instruction: On dual-compressor models, check that the refrigerator compressor is running. Listen for it at the rear or bottom of the unit.

whenToCallPro: If basic checks do not resolve EC02, call a Sub-Zero certified technician to diagnose compressor and sealed system issues.

faq.q: Can EC02 be caused by a power outage?
faq.a: Yes. After a power outage, it may take several hours for the refrigerator to cool back down. EC02 may clear on its own once temperature is restored.

fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the grille is not blocked by kitchen items. For built-in models, verify proper clearances per the installation guide (typically 1 inch minimum on sides).

fixSteps.title: Test the condenser fan
fixSteps.instruction: With power on, verify the condenser fan runs when the compressor runs. If the fan does not spin, check for obstructions or test the motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace the condenser fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power. Access the condenser fan motor, disconnect wiring and mounting hardware, and install the replacement.

fixSteps.instruction: Observe the door as it closes. It should close flush and evenly. If the door sags or does not align, the hinges may need adjustment.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the door gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Run your hand along the gasket with the door closed to feel for air leaks. Check for tears, warping, or debris preventing a tight seal.

fixSteps.title: Test the door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the door switch and test for proper operation. It should change state when the door opens and closes. Test continuity with a multimeter.

title: Freezer Sensor Failure
shortDescription: The freezer temperature sensor has failed or is reading out of range.
fullDescription: Error EC10 indicates the freezer compartment temperature sensor (thermistor) has either an open or shorted circuit. The control board cannot read the freezer temperature, preventing proper regulation of the freezer compressor and defrost cycles.

causes.cause: Sensor connector is disconnected or corroded
Sensor wiring damaged by frost or ice
Control board sensor input has failed

symptoms: Freezer temperature display shows dashes or error
Freezer runs continuously or not at all
Defrost cycle may not function properly

fixSteps.title: Access the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Open the freezer and remove the rear panel to access the sensor. On Sub-Zero built-in models, the sensor is typically clipped to the evaporator or wall.

fixSteps.title: Check the connector
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the sensor connector is firmly seated. Clean any frost or corrosion from the contacts.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the sensor and measure resistance. At 0F/-18C it should read approximately 16,000 ohms. At room temperature approximately 10,000 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the old sensor from its mount, disconnect wiring, and install the replacement in the same position.

whenToCallPro: If replacing the sensor does not clear EC10, the control board needs professional diagnosis.

title: Vacuum Condenser Sensor Failure
shortDescription: Vacuum condenser temperature sensor reports out-of-range value.
fullDescription: EC70 indicates the vacuum-insulated condenser thermistor is reading outside the expected range, preventing the control from regulating the sealed system efficiently.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the unit
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 5 minutes and restore power. Some EC70 events clear after a reset.

fixSteps.title: Inspect thermistor harness
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the lower grille and verify the condenser thermistor connector is fully seated.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure resistance; should read ~10kΩ at 77°F. Replace if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: If resistance is in spec but the code persists, the main control board likely needs Sub-Zero certified diagnosis.

faq.q: Will the fridge keep cooling with EC70?
faq.a: Yes, but the system runs in failsafe mode and may overcool or undercool. Resolve promptly to avoid compressor stress.
Sealed-system electronics are typically covered for 5 years on Sub-Zero built-in models.

title: Fresh Food Thermistor Drift
shortDescription: The fresh food compartment thermistor is drifting outside calibration limits.
fullDescription: EC71 is logged when the fresh-food thermistor produces a value that does not track with secondary sensors over a 30-minute window.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for moisture
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the thermistor cover near the top of the fresh food compartment and dry with a microfiber cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the two-pin connector and swap in a new thermistor; route harness clear of evaporator coils.

whenToCallPro: Persistent drift after replacement points to a UI board fault — schedule certified service.

faq.a: No — Sub-Zero thermistors are not field-calibrated; replacement is the supported repair.

title: Ice Maker Communication Loss
shortDescription: Main control lost communication with the ice maker module.
fullDescription: EC72 indicates a CAN-bus or harness break between the integrated ice maker and the main control. Ice production halts until communication is restored.

causes.cause: Ice maker harness pinched in door hinge

fixSteps.title: Inspect freezer harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open the freezer drawer fully and check the harness routing for chafing or pinch points.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ice maker connector
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the ice maker cover and reseat the 6-pin Molex connector.

whenToCallPro: If reseating fails to clear EC72, the ice maker module or the main board needs replacement by certified service.

faq.q: Will food in the freezer be safe?
faq.a: Yes — only the ice maker is offline; freezer cooling continues normally.

title: Dual Compressor Imbalance
shortDescription: Refrigeration and freezer compressors report mismatched run-times.
fullDescription: EC73 trips when one of the two compressors in dual-compressor models has logged 25% more runtime than the other over a 7-day window, suggesting a load imbalance.

causes.cause: Failing evaporator fan in one compartment

fixSteps.title: Audit door usage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the door alarm has not been muted and gaskets seat fully when closed.

fixSteps.title: Check evaporator fans
fixSteps.instruction: Listen at each compartment with the door switch defeated — both fans should run continuously during cooling demand.

whenToCallPro: If both fans run and gaskets are sound, contact Sub-Zero for refrigerant charge verification.

faq.a: No — it is a service hint that lets you address an imbalance before either compressor fails prematurely.

title: Dispenser Solenoid Stuck
shortDescription: Water dispenser solenoid did not return to the closed state.
fullDescription: EC74 is logged when the dispenser solenoid feedback shows continued flow more than 4 seconds after the actuator was released, often due to mineral buildup.
symptoms: Water continues briefly after releasing dispenser pad

fixSteps.title: Run vinegar through dispenser
fixSteps.instruction: Fill the reservoir with food-grade vinegar and dispense 1 quart to dissolve scale.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off the water supply, disconnect the inlet line and swap the dispenser solenoid valve.

whenToCallPro: If the solenoid is new and the code returns, the UI board may be holding the actuator line; call certified service.

faq.a: Yes — but address the leak before it stains cabinetry.

title: Air Purification Cartridge End-of-Life
shortDescription: The Sub-Zero air purification cartridge has expired and must be replaced.
fullDescription: EC75 is a maintenance reminder that the air purification cartridge has reached its 12-month service life. The fridge continues normal operation.

fixSteps.title: Replace cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Twist the cartridge counter-clockwise on the rear wall and install a new one. Reset reminder in service menu.

whenToCallPro: This is a user-replaceable maintenance item — service is rarely required.

faq.a: No, it is informational. Replacement keeps food fresher longer.

title: Water Filter Bypass Detected
shortDescription: The unit detects the water filter is in bypass position.
fullDescription: EC76 indicates the filter housing has been rotated to the bypass position rather than holding a cartridge, which is allowed but raises an advisory.

fixSteps.title: Verify filter installation
fixSteps.instruction: Twist a fresh filter cartridge clockwise until it stops; the indicator should change to ready.

whenToCallPro: Only call service if the filter is properly seated yet bypass remains shown.

faq.a: Yes — water flows directly without filtration. Replace with a cartridge for best taste.

title: Door Light LED Driver Fault
shortDescription: LED driver for compartment lighting reports an over-current event.
fullDescription: EC77 logs when the LED driver shuts down after detecting an over-current condition, typically from a damaged LED panel or harness.
symptoms: Lights flicker briefly then go dark

fixSteps.title: Inspect LED panel
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the LED panel cover and check for cracks or moisture damage.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and reconnect the LED harness; verify it is clear of door hinge.

whenToCallPro: If both panel and harness are sound but EC77 persists, the LED driver board needs professional replacement.

faq.a: No — only lighting is affected. Cooling continues normally.

title: Defrost Heater Open Circuit
shortDescription: Defrost heater circuit reports infinite resistance.
fullDescription: EC78 indicates the freezer defrost heater is open, preventing scheduled defrost cycles. Ice will eventually accumulate on the evaporator.

causes.cause: Open thermal fuse on defrost circuit

fixSteps.title: Verify thermal fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power, remove the rear evaporator panel and test the inline thermal fuse for continuity.

fixSteps.title: Test defrost heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across the heater terminals; expect 30-50 ohms. Replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Sealed-system access is involved; if you are not comfortable working near refrigerant lines, call Sub-Zero service.

faq.q: Can I just turn off auto-defrost?
faq.a: No — Sub-Zero models do not allow defrost to be disabled in user mode.

title: Touchscreen Calibration Drift
shortDescription: Capacitive touchscreen reports inputs without user contact.
fullDescription: EC79 fires when the touch controller detects ghost taps over a 60-second interval, often from moisture on the panel surface.

fixSteps.title: Clean touch panel
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe with a microfiber cloth dampened with isopropyl alcohol. Allow to dry fully.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle and recalibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the lock button for 10 seconds with a dry display to trigger touch recalibration.

whenToCallPro: If recalibration fails, the UI overlay must be replaced by certified service.

faq.q: Could a household cleaner cause this?
faq.a: Yes — sticky residues hold moisture. Stick to dilute alcohol or Sub-Zero approved cleaner.
